pr_title: ESQL: Skip multivalues in LOOKUP JOIN matches
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/118780

To follow the same logics of the `==` operator (Doesn't match or work at all on multivalues or nulls), we're removing the Lucene matching currently being  indirectly used by LOOKUP JOIN.

issue_context.title: ESQL: LOOKUP JOIN should warn when join keys are multi-valued
issue_context.body:
The current implementation of LOOKUP JOIN is treats multivalued join keys very leniently and just matches rows whenever any value in the left hand join key matches any value in the right hand join key (c.f. [tests here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/693bb794bce43eb20d07b08ceba5e796ded6efbd/x-pack/plugin/esql/qa/testFixtures/src/main/resources/lookup-join.csv-spec#L199-L227)).

That might not be the desired behavior long-term. Let's at least issue a warning in this case, and maybe also change the lookup operator(s) to not consider any multivalues as matching.
comments: There's still the other way failing (probably): Multivalues in the lookup index, matching single values. Reopening until it's reviewed and fixed

In addition to that, the current solution does not yet issue a warning to the user, does it? I can't see any warnings expected in the [csv tests](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/120519/files#diff-334f3328c5f066a093ed8a5ea4a62cd6bcdb304b660b15763bb4f64d0e87ed7cR438-R469).
Reopening for now as warnings are missing
